answer: An anti-Sybil scheme can use a spiral beacon chamber: each identity claims one turn of a spiral corridor and must periodically sound a beacon pulse whose echo returns after a delay fixed by that turn's path length. Neighbors listen and report the echo they heard, so a position counts only when independent listeners agree on the timing. One operator cannot fake dozens of echoes at once, since each turn yields a distinct delay no other turn can replay. Mass-produced accounts collapse into identical echoes and expose the farm, while genuine users build a history of consistent echoes.
